sentences.text: Mcmurdodus is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish, a group of animals with skeletons made of cartilage rather than bone, belonging to the family Mcmurdodontidae.
The genus was first described by White in 1968.
An Australian species originally named M. whitei was later moved to the new genus Maiseyodus in 2021.
Recent studies suggest the family Mcmurdodontidae is now considered indeterminate among chondrichthyans, the broader group of cartilaginous fish.
The species Mcmurdodus featherensis lived in Antarctica during the Middle Devonian period.
Scientists debate whether Mcmurdodus belongs to the Hexanchiformes because it lacks multiple layers of enameloid on its tooth crowns, a feature found in all modern sharks.
There is also disagreement regarding its classification because most divergence estimates for modern sharks do not align with the age of this genus.
